reviewed_invariants: The private fast path receives only validated Templates: read_artifact bounds slots to 32, fragments to slots+1, literal/sample sizes to 64 KiB, and reparses a null-filled skeleton to require identical fragment boundaries. PreparedSchema owns the validated result; no public constructor permits an unchecked Template.

Exact strip_prefix comparisons, the unchanged primitive_end parser, full-record UTF-8 validation and empty remaining input establish the same lexical layout and token slices. Truncation, invalid tokens, extra suffix bytes and invalid UTF-8 cannot partially emit output through a failed fast path.

The fixed 32-slot array and all slices are bounded by validated slot counts and parser endpoints. Record size limits bound index arithmetic; literal_len*2 is at most 128 KiB, and selected compact-record size is strictly less than the reserved literal-record allowance. The 16 MiB target and 65,536-record/fallback bounds remain unchanged.

On a proven first-template match, legacy lookup would encounter index 0 first even with a fingerprint collision. The fast path charges exactly twice the matching literal length and preserves terminal work-budget saturation and literal fallback. A speculative mismatch leaves both output and the legacy lookup budget unchanged.

Uncharged speculative matching inspects only one template per bounded record; prefix successes consume disjoint input and any failed prefix is bounded by remaining input. This adds bounded input-scanning work, not an unbounded template search. Nonmatching performance remains an empirical control rather than a guaranteed optimization.

The delta adds no unsafe code, executable recipe, dependency, authentication, decoder, cache-admission or publication change. Full original-byte identity and receiver commit checks remain outside this sender-only modification.
